review_locator: PMCID:PMC3753797, Receptor-type tyrosine phosphatases ligands review; PMCID:PMC7672882, Pleiotrophin: Activity and Mechanism
primary_title: Pleiotrophin signals increased tyrosine phosphorylation of beta-catenin through inactivation of the intrinsic catalytic activity of the receptor-type protein tyrosine phosphatase beta/zeta
decision_basis: The reviews identify PTPRZ1/RPTPbeta-zeta as the principal pleiotrophin receptor-like phosphatase; the cited primary study demonstrates PTN interaction with PTPRZ1 in U373-MG cells and ligand-dependent reduction of intrinsic phosphatase activity with increased beta-catenin tyrosine phosphorylation.
limitations_preserved: Preserve PTPRZ1 receptor-phosphatase inactivation and chondroitin-sulfate/GAG dependence; do not convert this inhibitory receptor interaction into a conventional kinase relay or SCI claim.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC3417803, Midkine, a heparin-binding cytokine with multiple roles in development, repair and diseases; PMCID:PMC3925020, Structure and function of midkine
primary_title: A receptor-like protein-tyrosine phosphatase PTPzeta/RPTPbeta binds a heparin-binding growth factor midkine: involvement of arginine 78 of midkine in the high affinity binding to PTPzeta
decision_basis: The reviews identify PTPRZ1/RPTPbeta-zeta as a high-affinity midkine receptor; the cited primary solid-phase binding and mutagenesis study maps high- and low-affinity MDK binding, identifies Arg78 as required for high-affinity receptor interaction, and links binding to neuronal migration induction.
limitations_preserved: Preserve chondroitin-sulfate-dependent receptor recognition and phosphatase-receptor context; binding/migration evidence does not establish a universal intracellular relay or SCI branch.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC3417803, Midkine, a heparin-binding cytokine with multiple roles in development, repair and diseases; PMCID:PMC3925020, Structure and function of midkine
primary_title: LDL receptor-related protein as a component of the midkine receptor
decision_basis: The reviews identify LRP1 as a midkine receptor component; the cited primary study isolates LRP from embryonic mouse membranes, measures direct MDK-LRP binding, and shows receptor-associated-protein-sensitive inhibition of MDK-dependent embryonic-neuron survival.
limitations_preserved: Preserve LRP1 as an endocytic/receptor-complex component and RAP-sensitive MDK binding; do not infer a canonical LRP1 kinase relay or traumatic-SCI receiver attribution.
